$comment: The Slack bot's whole permission surface. The bridge runs `claude -p --permission-mode dontAsk --setting-sources project` in this directory, so only this file (and managed settings) applies, plus the absolute-path read rules the bridge adds with --settings (bridge.py permission_overlay): anything not allowed is refused without asking, and every Bash call is vetted by ../bash_guard.py. Reads are an ALLOW-LIST: this workspace, the real skill directory (added by the bridge) and the saved triage files. A deny list can't do that job: its `**/.env` style patterns only match under this directory, so a .env anywhere else on the host stayed readable.

hooks.command: python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/../bash_guard.py" || { echo 'Blocked: the Bash guard did not run cleanly' >&2; exit 2; }
